alt.en: A colour photograph of the front of an old stone building with a stone-tiled roof. A gable holds a square sundial marked "Tempus fugit" and 1782; below it are leaded diamond-pane windows and a round-arched wooden door between fluted pilasters, with wooden benches and two potted shrubs on a lawn.
alt.es: Fotografía en color de la fachada de un antiguo edificio de piedra con tejado de losas. En el frontón hay un reloj de sol cuadrado con la inscripción "Tempus fugit" y el año 1782; debajo, ventanas de vidrieras en rombos y una puerta de madera con arco de medio punto entre pilastras acanaladas, con bancos de madera y dos arbustos en macetas sobre el césped.

caption.en: Sackville College, the almshouse at East Grinstead in Sussex where John Mason Neale was warden: the title page of his Mediaeval Hymns and Sequences (1851), the book with his English of this hymn, calls him "Warden of Sackville College".
caption.es: El Sackville College, el asilo de East Grinstead, en Sussex, del que John Mason Neale era director: la portada de su Mediaeval Hymns and Sequences (1851), el libro con su versión inglesa de este himno, lo llama "Warden of Sackville College" (director del Sackville College).

source: Sackville College, East Grinstead, main entrance (photograph, 12 February 2019)

alt.en: A printed book page, number 119, headed "Veni, Veni, Emmanuel" in blackletter type, with a short note beginning "This Advent Hymn is little more than a versification" and two verses beginning "Draw nigh, draw nigh, Emmanuel, And loose Thy captive Israel", each ending "Rejoice! rejoice! Emmanuel Is born for thee, O Israel!".
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro, número 119, con el encabezado "Veni, Veni, Emmanuel" en letra gótica, una nota breve que empieza "This Advent Hymn is little more than a versification" y dos estrofas que empiezan "Draw nigh, draw nigh, Emmanuel, And loose Thy captive Israel", cada una terminada en "Rejoice! rejoice! Emmanuel Is born for thee, O Israel!".

caption.en: John Mason Neale's English in his Mediaeval Hymns and Sequences (London, 1851), page 119: it opens "Draw nigh, draw nigh, Emmanuel", and his note calls the hymn "little more than a versification" of the O antiphons.
caption.es: El inglés de John Mason Neale en su Mediaeval Hymns and Sequences (Londres, 1851), página 119: empieza "Draw nigh, draw nigh, Emmanuel", y su nota llama al himno "poco más que una versificación" de las antífonas de la O.

source: J. M. Neale, Mediaeval Hymns and Sequences (London: Joseph Masters, 1851), p. 119, "Veni, Veni, Emmanuel"
library: University of California, Los Angeles (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1851 (title page "MDCCCLI"); Neale died 1866. Internet Archive record: "possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT", "no visible notice of copyright; stated date is 1851". Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of California, Los Angeles, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed hymn page numbered 131, headed "65 (or 30)", "Veni, veni Emmanuel", "Advent" and "From a French Missal in the National Library, Lisbon", with the tune in square plainsong notes on four-line staves and five verses under it, beginning "Draw nigh, draw nigh, Em-man-u-el, And ransom captive Is-ra-el".
alt.es: Página impresa de himnario, número 131, con el encabezado "65 (or 30)", "Veni, veni Emmanuel", "Advent" y "From a French Missal in the National Library, Lisbon", con la melodía en notas cuadradas de canto llano sobre pentagramas de cuatro líneas y cinco estrofas debajo, que empiezan "Draw nigh, draw nigh, Em-man-u-el, And ransom captive Is-ra-el".

caption.en: The Hymnal Noted, Part II (London, 1856), page 131, in a later printing: Neale's revised words under the tune VENI EMMANUEL, credited to "a French Missal in the National Library, Lisbon", a missal never found.
caption.es: The Hymnal Noted, Part II (Londres, 1856), página 131, en una impresión posterior: la letra revisada de Neale bajo la melodía VENI EMMANUEL, atribuida a "un misal francés de la Biblioteca Nacional de Lisboa", un misal que nunca se encontró.

source: The Hymnal Noted, Parts I. and II. (London: Novello, Ewer and Co.), Part II, p. 131, No. 65 (or 30), "Veni, veni Emmanuel"
library: Google Books scan (holding library not named), via the Internet Archive
licenceEvidence: Internet Archive record licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark). Part II dated 1856 on its title page; this printing under the Novello, Ewer and Co. imprint (used from 1867). Neale died 1866, Helmore died 1890 (see rights.md). The scanner's "Digitized by Google" mark is cropped away.
credit: Google Books scan, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: The top of a printed hymnal page headed "Advent": the last line of a hymn tune in four parts on two staves, ending "A-men", the text "The Redeemer shall come to Zion", and five verses in two columns beginning "O come, O come, Emmanuel, And ransom captive Israel", with the marks mf, p, cr and ff beside the lines.
alt.es: Parte superior de una página impresa de himnario con el encabezado "Advent": la última línea de una melodía de himno a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, que termina en "A-men", el texto "The Redeemer shall come to Zion" y cinco estrofas en dos columnas que empiezan "O come, O come, Emmanuel, And ransom captive Israel", con las marcas mf, p, cr y ff junto a los versos.

caption.en: Hymn 49 in the Revised Edition of Hymns Ancient and Modern (1875), page 35, in a later printing: the words "O come, O come, Emmanuel" as we sing them, with the dynamics the edition printed beside each line.
caption.es: El himno 49 de la edición revisada de Hymns Ancient and Modern (1875), página 35, en una impresión posterior: la letra "O come, O come, Emmanuel" tal como la cantamos, con la dinámica (matices) que la edición imprimió junto a cada verso.

source: Hymns Ancient and Modern for Use in the Services of the Church, with Accompanying Tunes, Revised Edition (London: William Clowes and Sons; undated later printing, catalogued 1874), Hymn 49, p. 35
library: Harold B. Lee Library, Brigham Young University (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Revised Edition, preface dated 21 January 1875; this printing undated (catalogued 1874). Words: Neale (died 1866) as altered by the compilers under H. W. Baker (died 1877); harmony W. H. Monk (died 1889). All rights ended long ago in the US, EU and Israel (see rights.md).
